feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: Learn2Play Bench: How Well Do LLM Agents Learn from Experience in Unfamiliar Environments?
entry.summary:
Learn2Play Bench evaluates LLM agents' ability to learn from experience using text-based games with novel or counterintuitive rules that prevent reliance on pretrained knowledge.

Why it matters: It establishes a controlled framework to isolate real-time experience-based learning from static pretrained knowledge, guiding better agent architectural designs.

entry.title: TokenRouter: Efficient Serving System for Token-Level LLM Routing
entry.summary:
TokenRouter is an open-source serving system designed for token-level LLM routing that resolves step desynchronization and batch admission delays to boost decoding throughput by 2.01–64.15x over existing serving systems.

Why it matters: It makes fine-grained, token-level LLM routing computationally viable for production deployment, significantly shifting the cost-quality Pareto frontier without sacrificing inference system throughput.

entry.title: MiMo-V2.6: Scaling Reinforcement Learning Towards Self-Improvement
entry.summary:
The MiMo-V2.6 series introduces scaled reinforcement learning for self-improvement across omni-modal foundation models using frozen MoE routers, massive batch throughput, groupwise agentic grading, and multi-domain agentic environments.

Why it matters: It demonstrates how to scale RL compute stably across diverse agentic domains and massive contexts to advance foundation model self-improvement.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Egocentric World Model with Fine-Grained Embodied Interaction
entry.summary:
ME-World is a multi-agent egocentric world model that generates synchronized first-person video streams based on agents' fine-grained embodied actions in a shared environment.

Why it matters: It enables more realistic and synchronized multi-agent physical simulations by maintaining fine-grained interaction, pose, and environmental consistency across multiple simultaneous first-person perspectives.

entry.title: OuroWorld: Bringing Any 3D World Alive as Diverse, Endlessly Looping 3D Cinemagraphs
entry.summary:
OuroWorld is a mask-free framework that transforms static 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes into endlessly looping, multi-view 3D cinemagraphs with diverse, seamless motion.

Why it matters: It enables the creation of dynamic, endlessly looping 3D scenes from static 3D representations without restricting motion types to simple fluid dynamics.

entry.title: Foundations of Large Language Models
entry.summary:
A foundational textbook structured into six core chapters covering pre-training, generative models, prompting, alignment, inference, and reasoning in large language models.

Why it matters: It provides a structured educational framework and technical reference for foundational concepts across the full life cycle of large language models.

entry.title: TestPrism: Rethinking Test Evaluation Beyond a Single Reference
entry.summary:
TestPrism is a benchmark that evaluates LLM test generation against multiple candidate implementations using the Joint Success Function, exposing severe overestimation in single-reference evaluations.

Why it matters: Evaluating LLM-generated tests against only a single reference program overstates test suite quality and masks faulty assertions, brittle checks, and missed edge cases.

entry.title: MC-Sparse: Deconstructing and Closing the Dense-Sparse Attention Gap in Diffusion Transformers
entry.summary:
MC-Sparse is a training-free sparse attention framework that caches exact token metadata and output residuals across denoising steps to accelerate diffusion transformers with negligible quality loss.

Why it matters: It enables faster video and high-resolution 3D generation by significantly reducing diffusion transformer latency without sacrificing visual fidelity or requiring costly model retraining.

entry.title: Beyond Spatio-Temporal Priors: A Generalizable Approach for Dense Correspondence Matching
entry.summary:
FreeMatching is a generalizable dense correspondence framework that combines generative and semantic foundation representations with teacher-guided iterative refinement to handle non-rigid, non-continuous transformations in image editing and reference-guided generation.

Why it matters: It enables accurate dense feature matching across complex generative transformations while serving as a reliable metric for identity preservation.

entry.title: LEGO: A Lifting-Free Approach for Exocentric-to-Egocentric Video Generation
entry.summary:
LEGO introduces a lifting-free framework that uses a fine-tuned LVSM-style transformer to directly synthesize egocentric structure from exocentric video, bypassing depth estimation and point-cloud reprojection for video diffusion models.

Why it matters: It eliminates the error propagation of explicit 3D reprojection in cross-view video generation, providing a more robust conditioning strategy for generative models under extreme viewpoint changes.

entry.title: U-Space: Uncovering When and Why Uncertainty Arises in Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers developed U-Space, a low-dimensional, training-free subspace constructed from semantic anchors that projects intermediate language model states into interpretable, token-level uncertainty maps and scalable confidence scores.

Why it matters: It enables real-time, interpretable uncertainty quantification directly from intermediate model states without the computational overhead of repeated generations or separate classifier training.

entry.title: Memento 3: Model-Based Recursive Self-Improvement through Reflective Rulebooks
entry.summary:
Memento 3 enables frozen LLM agents to achieve recursive self-improvement by iteratively refining natural-language rulebooks, compiling them into executable world-model code, and accepting updates verified via cell-exact replay without updating model weights.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that frozen LLMs can continuously learn and adapt to complex, dynamic environments purely through external code-compiled memory and verification loops.

entry.title: OneSearch-VL: Unified Multimodal Deep Research Agent for Image and Video
entry.summary:
OneSearch-VL is a unified multimodal agent that uses a Visually Grounded Evidence Graph (VGEG) to standardise data synthesis, process supervision, and evaluation across single-image, multi-image, and video deep research tasks.

Why it matters: It establishes a unified graph-based framework for visual grounding and external retrieval that significantly enhances multimodal deep research capabilities across static images and video.

entry.title: OmniCapBench: A Deep-Structured Evaluation Framework for Fine-Grained Audio-Visual Captioning
entry.summary:
OmniCapBench introduces a deep-structured evaluation framework for fine-grained audio-visual captioning using 786 densely annotated videos to convert free-form captions into sets of atomic, verifiable evaluation units.

Why it matters: It provides a reliable, fine-grained diagnostic tool that pinpoints specific perceptual and cross-modal reasoning failures in multimodal LLMs beyond what unconstrained judges or holistic scores capture.

entry.title: ViSkill: Reinforcing VLM Agents with Evolving Visual-Native Skills
entry.summary:
ViSkill is a visual-native skill learning framework that encodes successful VLM trajectories into visual skill cards, creating a closed-loop system where skill accumulation and policy optimization continuously reinforce each other.

Why it matters: By maintaining spatial geometric structure in visual skills and coupling skill retrieval directly with policy rewards, VLM agents can learn complex spatial tasks with higher sample efficiency and accuracy.

entry.title: Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervision
entry.summary:
Multi-Agent Self-Supervision (MASS) enables recursive self-improvement on non-verifiable tasks by alternating evolutionary workflow optimization over multi-agent topologies with supervised fine-tuning on self-generated trajectories.

Why it matters: MASS provides a scalable method for self-improving LLMs on open-ended tasks where human evaluation bottlenecks exist, optimizing both execution tokens and downstream fine-tuning efficiency.

entry.title: Learning to Plan by Looking Back: Hindsight Hierarchies for Training Reasoning Models
entry.summary:
A self-improvement loop trains reasoning models by extracting hindsight solution ideas from solved problems to jointly supervise idea generation, reverse-engineering, and guided problem-solving.

Why it matters: It offers a framework for reasoning models to learn from problems beyond their current capability by using known solutions as retrospectives to bootstrap planning skills.

entry.title: When KL Regularization Misfires in Group Policy Optimization
entry.summary:
Researchers identify seven failure modes in reference-policy KL regularization during group policy optimization and introduce Zero-Sum Calibrated Policy Optimization (ZCPO) to calibrate within-group reward coefficients using conditional KL.

Why it matters: ZCPO prevents policy degradation caused by standard KL regularization flaws, allowing more stable and effective reinforcement learning for group policy optimization.

entry.title: Rehearse Everything, Remember Nothing: Attic-KV Rehearses What Will Be Read
entry.summary:
Attic-KV is a training-free KV cache compression method that replaces full context rereading with self-quizzing via question-answer pairs quoting the context and content-adaptive anchor tokens.

Why it matters: It significantly improves LLM retention and retrieval accuracy in low-budget KV cache compression scenarios without requiring model retraining.

entry.title: GRPODropout: Less is More for Online Reinforcement Learning Rollouts
entry.summary:
GRPODropout prevents policy entropy collapse in online LLM reinforcement learning by selectively dropping a small subset of high-probability positive-advantage rollouts before updating the policy.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that selectively filtering out redundant positive rollouts improves exploration and performance in LLM reasoning tasks without increasing training costs.

entry.title: Easy to anticipate, hard to compute: boundary dependence finds the computed outputs that entropy patching misses
entry.summary:
BLT's entropy-based patching misses low-entropy, compute-intensive byte positions like math solutions, but a label-free boundary-dependence signal restores patch allocation and downstream accuracy under tight budgets.

Why it matters: Relying solely on next-byte entropy for dynamic patching causes severe performance degradation on reasoning tasks, which can be fixed using unsupervised boundary dependence.

entry.title: DIAL-OPD: Learning More from Fewer Tokens in On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
DIAL-OPD introduces a token-selection method for on-policy distillation that weights log-ratio rewards using the logarithmic mean of teacher and student probabilities to filter uninformative tokens.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that selective token filtering can improve distillation efficiency and performance simultaneously, outperforming full-token supervision while using a smaller teacher model.

entry.title: Caught in the Act: Probes Effectively Detect Sabotage and Catch Unverbalized Deception
entry.summary:
Researchers created a novel multi-layer, multi-token probe architecture and the FIBS dataset, achieving up to 98.8% AUC in SHADE-Arena to detect LLM agent deception and sabotage.

Why it matters: White-box probing provides a scalable, high-accuracy alternative to black-box text monitoring for detecting hidden agent goals and unverbalized model deception.

entry.title: Predicting Alignment Generalization with Value Representations
entry.summary:
Researchers established the task of alignment generalization prediction, showing that model activation representations predict cross-value behavior changes significantly better than text-description baselines.

Why it matters: Predicting how narrow alignment training impacts unobserved behaviors enables more empirical, robust design of LLM post-training targets.

entry.title: LeWAM: A JEPA World Action Model with Diffusion-Steering-Based MPC
entry.summary:
LeWAM is an end-to-end, decoder-free JEPA world action model using a bidirectional transformer that improves latent state representation, closed-loop acting, and noise-space MPC planning.

Why it matters: By replacing noisy reconstruction-based latents with a multi-mode JEPA representation and planning in noise space, LeWAM unifies robust world modeling and policy execution without susceptibility to model exploitation.

entry.title: Recursive Game Creator: An Agentic Product-Level Experience-Oriented Game Harness
entry.summary:
Recursive Game Creator is an agentic harness that iteratively refines game prototypes into engaging games using a four-agent loop composed of a Designer, Builder, Player, and Reviewer.

Why it matters: It establishes a programmatic, player-trajectory-driven evaluation framework that improves the entertainment value and runtime reliability of AI-generated games.

entry.title: GRACE: Generation-aware latent compression for efficient video generation
entry.summary:
GRACE is a two-stage framework that compresses pretrained video autoencoders while maintaining compatibility with pretrained Diffusion Transformers through residual latent learning, DiT feature alignment, and asymmetric denoising.

Why it matters: It enables order-of-magnitude inference speedups for large video diffusion models without requiring expensive retrain-from-scratch cycles or sacrificing generation quality.

entry.title: VepAgent: Bridging Causal-Transition via Tool-Augmented Reinforcement Learning for Video Event Prediction
entry.summary:
VepAgent improves Video Event Prediction by using supervised fine-tuning on a novel dataset, a diagnostic tool library, and composite reward reinforcement learning to model unobserved causal transitions.

Why it matters: It enables multimodal LLMs to actively ground future event predictions in verified visual evidence rather than relying on retrospective text summarization and hallucinated priors.

entry.title: RunningTab: Direct Workspace Interaction with Environment-Side Tabs
entry.summary:
RunningTab is a framework that improves direct workspace interaction (DWI) for LLM agents by introducing an environment-side tab to track task requirements, read excerpts, and unopened candidate files.

Why it matters: Environment-side tracking prevents LLM agents from missing critical information or omitting required components when generating complex deliverables from local file repositories.

entry.title: UltraText Bench: A Comprehensive Bilingual Benchmark for Evaluating Visual Text Rendering in Image Generation
entry.summary:
UltraText Bench is a new bilingual benchmark evaluating dense visual text rendering across 432 English and Chinese prompts, using the Q-Judger vision-language model to score text fidelity, clarity, spatial quality, and scene quality.

Why it matters: It provides a rigorous framework to stress-test and quantify how well image generation models sustain multi-region, dense text legibility and spatial accuracy as text rendering workloads scale.

entry.title: RobotWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Robot Use Across Diverse Tasks and Embodiments
entry.summary:
RobotWorld is a simulation benchmark featuring 84 tasks across five embodiment types to evaluate multimodal agents converting instructions into physical robot execution.

Why it matters: It exposes the composition failures preventing multimodal AI agents from reliably translating digital tool use into physical physical-world control across diverse robotic platforms.

entry.title: Gains and Collapse in On-Policy Distillation:A Reinforcement Learning Perspective
entry.summary:
This paper analyzes On-Policy Distillation (OPD) through a reinforcement learning perspective, revealing that OPD works by amplifying student behaviors favored by the teacher's implicit rewards rather than expanding student capabilities.

Why it matters: Understanding OPD as implicit reward feedback shifts distillation focus toward the teacher's evaluation reliability rather than its generation quality, offering concrete fixes for generation collapse.

entry.title: SWE-Game: Can Coding Agents Build the Games We Want?
entry.summary:
SWE-Game is a new benchmark featuring 247 tasks across 41 Godot games to evaluate AI coding agents on 2D and 3D game development and repair.

Why it matters: It establishes a rigorous, execution-based framework for measuring AI agents' ability to implement complex, interactive software systems like game engines.

entry.title: PhysEvo: Astra Can Act, Let It
entry.summary:
PhysEvo enables physical recursive self-improvement around a single frozen model by using a meta-agent to iteratively revise tools, skills, and diagnostic capabilities based on task execution trajectories.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that frozen foundation models can achieve complex robotic manipulation and self-correction purely through persistent, testable harness and skill revisions without expensive retrainings.

entry.title: Inverting Multi-Vector Visual Document Indices
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrated that multi-vector visual document indices can be inverted via conditional image generation to reconstruct readable document pages and recover sensitive tokens directly from stored patch vectors.

Why it matters: Multi-vector visual document indices contain sufficient spatial and semantic information to reconstruct confidential source documents, requiring vector databases to be secured with the same safeguards as raw documents.

entry.title: Minimal Witness Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
Minimal-Witness Reinforcement Learning (MWRL) is a new RL framework that identifies complete families of irreducible, sufficient conditions by crediting proposed sets based on the coverage lost without them.

Why it matters: MWRL enables reinforcement learning models to discover diverse, non-redundant alternative explanations and mechanisms rather than converging on a single optimal solution.

entry.title: NAMVIS: Next-Scale Autoregressive Multi-View Image Synthesis
entry.summary:
NAMVIS is a diffusion-free, geometry-conditioned next-scale autoregressive framework for sparse-view novel view synthesis that achieves higher image quality and 3x faster generation than diffusion baselines.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that autoregressive token prediction can replace slow, iterative diffusion processes for 3D view synthesis, substantially reducing inference latency without sacrificing visual fidelity.

entry.title: From Pareto to Preference: Personalized Test-Time Scaling via Amortized Agentic Policy Discovery
entry.summary:
PersonTTS is an amortized agentic policy-discovery framework that optimizes personalized test-time scaling by reusing search experience to satisfy multi-dimensional user constraints across accuracy, latency, and cost.

Why it matters: It enables flexible, automated deployment of large language models by tailoring inference compute budgets to complex, real-world combinations of cost, latency, and accuracy constraints.

entry.title: On-Policy Distillation with Negative-Policy Rollouts
entry.summary:
Negative-Policy On-Policy Distillation (NP-OPD) integrates rollouts from a lower-capability negative reference policy alongside teacher supervision to provide explicit negative signals during student model training.

Why it matters: NP-OPD enhances student model performance in post-training distillation by leveraging negative policy rollouts to expose and correct low-quality outputs that standard teacher supervision misses.

entry.title: QuadTok: Quadtree Visual Tokenizer for Autoregressive Image Generation
entry.summary:
QuadTok introduces a hierarchical quadtree visual tokenizer and autoregressive model that dynamically allocates tokens based on image complexity, reducing token count while maintaining reconstruction quality.

Why it matters: It improves the computational efficiency of autoregressive image generation models by reducing total sequence length without sacrificing reconstruction quality or spatial control.

entry.title: Decoupling Exploration from Optimization in RLVR
entry.summary:
Exploration-Distillation (ExpDis) improves RLVR by decoupling novelty-incentivized trajectory generation from student policy optimization through an iterative explore-filter-distill pipeline.

Why it matters: It enables aggressive exploration in RLVR without compromising model quality, yielding language models that generate more diverse correct solutions for complex reasoning tasks.

entry.title: Composing What Each Teacher Learned: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation through Teacher-Relative Shifts
entry.summary:
Delta-MOPD improves multi-teacher on-policy distillation by isolating post-training logit shifts from inherited base model preferences and re-anchoring them to the student initialization.

Why it matters: It establishes target signal construction as a crucial, independent design parameter in multi-teacher distillation, improving multi-domain post-training alignment without changing teacher selection.

entry.title: A Good Self-Teacher Meets the Student Where They Are: Joint On-Policy Learning and Teaching
entry.summary:
JOLT derives theoretical conditions for optimal self-distillation and jointly trains a single policy as both a privileged teacher with KL regularization and an unprivileged student receiving dense on-policy updates.

Why it matters: JOLT solves sparse-reward bottlenecks in long-horizon reasoning tasks by generating dense, alignment-safe self-supervision without relying on a larger external teacher model.

entry.title: Training Parallel Speculative Draft Models by Directly Minimizing Expected Decoding Rounds
entry.summary:
Researchers formulated speculative decoding as a Markov reward process to train parallel draft models by directly minimizing Expected Decoding Rounds (EDR) via exact temporal-difference gradients.

Why it matters: Directly optimizing expected decoding rounds eliminates sub-optimal surrogate training objectives, maximizing draft model efficiency and accelerating overall target LLM inference.

entry.title: Reasoning-Token Spikes Under Prompted Untruthful Responding in Large Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrated that large language models generate significantly more reasoning tokens when prompted to produce untruthful responses compared to truthful ones, establishing token count as a content-independent indicator of untruthful behavior.

Why it matters: Reasoning-token counts provide a simple, content-independent metric to help detect untruthful model behavior when chain-of-thought traces are unfaithful, illegible, or hidden by provider APIs.

entry.title: Open-MMUnlearning: Unifying Methods and Evaluation for MLLM Unlearning
entry.summary:
Open-MMUnlearning is a new open-source framework unifying MLLM unlearning methods, data processing, and evaluation across 12 unlearning techniques, 8 models, and 5 safety, privacy, and copyright benchmarks.

Why it matters: It establishes a standardized, reproducible benchmark to reliably measure and compare how effectively multimodal models can remove sensitive data without sacrificing overall utility.

entry.title: SLDR: Defending Against Malicious Fine-tuning via Selective Layers Recovery and Dynamic Routing
entry.summary:
SLDR defends fine-tuned LLMs against safety alignment degradation using selective layer-wise LoRA recovery adapters and representation-based dynamic routing inference.

Why it matters: SLDR provides a robust defense mechanism for Fine-tuning-as-a-service providers to prevent malicious safety alignment erosion without sacrificing downstream task performance.

entry.title: Fault-tolerant foundation models
entry.summary:
LLMs can be trained to tolerate faulty, low-energy hardware, demonstrating increased error resilience as model scale grows without infinite overhead.

Why it matters: Enabling fault-tolerant LLM inference on energy-efficient, unreliable hardware offers a viable path to substantially reduce AI energy consumption.

entry.title: SemanticFold: Latent Sequence Compression SeparatesLanguage Modeling, Decodability, and Reasoning
entry.summary:
SemanticFold introduces a latent prefix compression scheme to evaluate how sequence folding impacts language modeling likelihood, probe decodability, reasoning accuracy, and latency across five model scales using a fixed-target protocol.

Why it matters: The findings demonstrate that sequence compression impacts language model fit, representation decodability, and downstream reasoning non-monotonically, proving that no single scalar metric can validate compressed latent states.

entry.title: Which Rollout Taught It That? BehaviorTrace and the Limits of Training-Data Attribution in Online RL
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce BehaviorTrace, an evaluation harness showing that existing training-data attribution methods in online RL with GRPO are heavily biased by confounds like gradient magnitude and model fluency.

Why it matters: The findings demonstrate that current RL attribution methods largely reflect uninformative confounds rather than true causality, necessitating rigorous controls for gradient size and fluency when evaluating training-data attribution.

entry.title: Rethinking Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation: From Alignment Coverage to Supervision Reliability
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that cross-tokenizer on-policy distillation achieves optimal performance using compact, reliable supervision at strictly aligned token positions rather than maximizing full sequence alignment coverage.

Why it matters: Prioritizing supervision reliability over complete alignment coverage reduces computational overhead and prevents training instability caused by conflicting gradient signals in cross-tokenizer model compression.

entry.title: TRACE: Rollout-Guided Quantization-Aware Training for FP4 Reinforcement Learning of MoE Language Models
entry.summary:
TRACE is an FP4 quantization framework for Mixture-of-Experts language models that aligns train and rollout execution paths using rollout-guided quantization-aware training and deep-layer quantization-information caching.

Why it matters: It enables significantly faster and lower-memory RL post-training of large MoE models without sacrificing model performance compared to full BF16 execution.

entry.title: From Evidence to Action: How Tool-Using Agents Fail
entry.summary:
SafeActBench evaluates tool-using agents across 656 operational cases to reveal how the evidence-to-action chain fails across static judgment and multi-action workflows.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that agent safety and reliability cannot be measured by outcome correctness or static benchmark performance alone, requiring strict tracking of evidence dependencies during execution.

entry.title: World Action Learning via Interaction-Centric Spectral Latent Guidance
entry.summary:
WING is a framework that transfers human interaction knowledge from egocentric videos to robot policies using interaction-centric video decomposition and spectral latent action guidance.

Why it matters: It enables scalable robot policy training by efficiently transferring physical manipulation skills directly from abundant human egocentric video without requiring expensive robot-only demonstrations.

entry.title: HuatuoGPT-3: RL-Only Domain Adaptation from Base Models
entry.summary:
HuatuoGPT-3 uses One-stage Policy Optimization (OnePO) to enable RL-only domain adaptation directly from base LLMs, skipping the SFT phase entirely.

Why it matters: OnePO eliminates the need for a preliminary SFT stage in domain adaptation, streamlining optimization while preserving policy exploration diversity.

entry.title: UNREAL: Unifying Retrieval and Long-Context with a Single Model
entry.summary:
UNREAL is a parameter-efficient framework adding under 500K parameters to a frozen LLM, unifying corpus retrieval and long-context evidence selection using the model's internal representations.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that a single, parameter-light model-internal mechanism can replace separate retriever-reranker pipelines while making long-context LLM inference faster and more accurate.

entry.title: AGO AI Quality Gate: Evidence-First Release Decisions for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
entry.summary:
AGO is an evidence-first quality-gate framework for industrial RAG deployments that uses a four-state decision model, stratified beta-binomial risk quantification, layered scoring, and mandatory judge meta-evaluation.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that point estimates from low-cost LLM judges are insufficient for release decisions, requiring per-engagement meta-evaluation and probabilistic gating to prevent unsafe enterprise RAG deployments.

entry.title: MiniCorp: The Last Mile of the AI Agent Firm
entry.summary:
MiniCorp is an office simulator that models internal agent collaboration and external market dynamics to generate scalable longitudinal and counterfactual enterprise data.

Why it matters: It addresses the scarcity and privacy constraints of real-world enterprise data by providing a realistic, counterfactual environment for training and evaluating autonomous AI-run companies.

entry.title: GUI-HARVEST: Self-Improving GUI Agents through Evidence-Driven Harness Evolution
entry.summary:
GUI-HARVEST is an automatic framework that self-improves GUI agents with frozen backbone models by evolving their execution harnesses through visual groundings, multi-run comparison, and targeted source-code edits.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that GUI agent performance can be significantly improved solely by optimizing runtime execution harnesses without modifying or retraining underlying backbone models.

entry.title: NeMo-DCR: Bit-Exact Delta-Compressed Refit for Scalable Agentic RL at Trillion-Parameter Scale
entry.summary:
NeMo-DCR enables bit-exact delta-compressed policy refitting for trillion-parameter agentic RL by transmitting only modified weights across clusters without cross-cluster collectives.

Why it matters: It eliminates the network bottleneck of full-checkpoint transfers during agentic RL training, making cross-cluster weight synchronization practical at trillion-parameter scale.

entry.title: DiffGate: Difficulty-Gated Teacher Guidance for On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
DiffGate combines GRPO with outcome-gated, bounded teacher guidance applied exclusively to failed trajectories and scaled by group difficulty during on-policy distillation.

Why it matters: DiffGate provides dense token-level credit assignment for failed rollouts in RLVR without sacrificing outcome alignment, consistently boosting solution coverage across code and math tasks.

entry.title: DAEDALUS: Bootstrapping Agent Memory from Self-Generated Tasks
entry.summary:
DAEDALUS bootstraps reusable LLM agent memory through a dual-agent self-play architecture without requiring human guidelines, existing training tasks, or oracle verifiers.

Why it matters: It enables LLM agents to autonomously learn and transfer operational knowledge in new environments without human intervention or pre-existing annotated tasks.

entry.title: Understanding and Enhancing Backdoor Persistency in LLM Agent Post-Training
entry.summary:
Researchers developed PersistBD, a method that enables backdoors in third-party LLM agents to survive developer-led SFT and RL post-training.

Why it matters: This highlights a critical supply-chain security vulnerability where adversaries can craft persistent backdoors in open-source base models that survive standard developer fine-tuning pipelines.

entry.title: DistScene: Object-to-Scene Distillation for 3D Scene Generation
entry.summary:
DistScene is a 3D scene generation framework that jointly models explicit environment components and individual objects using Object-to-Scene Distillation from synthetic rendered scenes.

Why it matters: It improves single-image 3D scene reconstruction quality and spatial coherence by explicitly modeling background environment geometry alongside object-level priors.

entry.title: Harness-Aware Distillation for Small Language Model Agents
entry.summary:
Harness-Aware Distillation (HAD) improves small agent distillation by isolating teacher capabilities specific to harness interaction rather than blindly imitating full output sequences.

Why it matters: HAD enables smaller language models to act as effective agents under fixed deployment software without requiring labeled success metrics or reward models during distillation.

entry.title: How Much Evidence Should a Coding Agent's Self-Correction Carry? Adaptive Dirichlet Evidence for Self-Distillation
entry.summary:
Effective-Evidence Self-Distillation (EESD) improves coding agent correction learning by using Dirichlet posteriors to separate execution transition support from total evidence mass, generating uncertainty-penalized weights for KL-anchored updates.

Why it matters: Decoupling evidence support from evidence mass enables coding agents to weight execution feedback more accurately, improving downstream program correction performance.

entry.title: Rethinking Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation: From Alignment Coverage to Supervision Reliability
entry.summary:
A study on cross-tokenizer On-Policy Distillation reveals that compact reverse KL supervision at strictly aligned 1:1 token positions outperforms broader alignment schemes that include unreliable span-level log-probability signals.

Why it matters: Prioritizing supervision reliability over maximum token alignment coverage allows for more effective cross-tokenizer knowledge distillation while avoiding noisy, conflicting gradient signals.

entry.title: Denoising Hierarchical Representations: Joint Continuous Diffusion for Language Modeling
entry.summary:
Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models (H-CDLMs) improve continuous DLMs by jointly diffusing token embeddings alongside coarser semantic clusters with per-modality samplers and schedules.

Why it matters: It establishes a lightweight, parallel multi-granularity diffusion framework that allows continuous diffusion models to outperform existing continuous and discrete DLMs on standard language modeling benchmarks.

entry.title: When Forgetting is not Catastrophic: On the Mechanics of Spurious Forgetting
entry.summary:
Researchers show that language model forgetting consists of reversible access loss and irreversible erosion, where temporary collapse during finetuning can be undone by removing a single weight update direction.

Why it matters: Understanding that early forgetting is often a reversible representation shift allows practitioners to recover lost knowledge from finetuned models without full retraining.

entry.title: Random Feature Gaussian Process Attention: Linear-Time Probabilistic Attention with Calibrated Uncertainty
entry.summary:
The Random Fourier Feature Gaussian Process Attention (RFF-GPA) module uses low-rank kernel approximations to achieve linear-time computational complexity while providing calibrated uncertainty estimates in Transformers.

Why it matters: It enables scalable, well-calibrated uncertainty estimation in long-sequence Transformer models required for safety-critical applications.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning for Hierarchical Reasoning Rewards: Minimax-Optimal Rates with Transformers
entry.summary:
A theoretical study proves that on-policy Transformer actor-critic RL post-training achieves minimax-optimal regret rates for hierarchical rewards, whereas offline sampling from a fixed reference policy decays at a logarithmic rate.

Why it matters: The work provides a theoretical foundation showing how on-policy exploration progressively focuses sampling on reward-dense regions, mathematically justifying its superiority over offline post-training techniques.

entry.title: PHBA: Prefix-State Hybrid Block Attention
entry.summary:
Prefix-State Hybrid Block Attention (PHBA) replaces sliding-window attention in hybrid sequence models with top-k block-sparse retrieval coupled with compact prefix states generated by gated linear recurrences at block boundaries.

Why it matters: It enables exact, long-range token retrieval beyond fixed local windows without losing historical context or sacrificing training and inference efficiency.

entry.title: UNREAL: Unifying Retrieval and Long-Context with a Single Model
entry.summary:
UNREAL is a model-native evidence selection framework that unifies corpus retrieval and long-context inference by deriving queries and encoding chunks using frozen LLM internal representations with under 500K trainable parameters.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that a single parameter-efficient mechanism native to the LLM can outperform dedicated retriever-rerankers and optimize long-context inference compute.

entry.title: VETTA: Coordinating Turn- and Token-Level Credit Assignment for Multi-Turn LLM Agents
entry.summary:
VETTA is a multi-turn LLM agent credit-assignment method that coordinates turn- and token-level values using a lightweight shared critic with dual heads.

Why it matters: It improves LLM agent training performance under sparse feedback while significantly reducing critic compute costs.

entry.title: Towards In-Parameter Memory Augmentation for Large Language Models
entry.summary:
This survey taxonomy categorizes in-parameter memory augmentation for LLMs across two axes: Parameter Placement (Embedding, Attention, FFN, or Hybrid) and Parameter Acquisition Time (offline versus online deployment).

Why it matters: It provides a structured taxonomy for extending LLM knowledge capacity without consuming context windows or incurring repeated context encoding costs during inference.

entry.title: Memadapter: Counterfactual Adaptation Against Memory-induced Sycophancy
entry.summary:
MemAdapter is a novel framework that uses counterfactual reasoning and context-aware reflection to mitigate memory-induced sycophancy in LLM agents without needing to alter or purge valid persistent memories.

Why it matters: It prevents long-term memory systems in LLM agents from forcing uncritical alignment with user bias without requiring aggressive memory filtering.

entry.title: Optimizing the Optimizer: Language Models Discover Faster Molecular Relaxation
entry.summary:
An LLM-based autoresearch agent optimized the open-source Sella molecular geometry optimizer, yielding the AutoSella family that reduces required force-evaluation calls across unseen molecules and potentials.

Why it matters: Automating optimizer code design via language models significantly cuts the computationally expensive force-evaluation calls required for quantum-chemical geometry optimization.

entry.title: In-Distribution Forcing for Long Video Generation at Test Time
entry.summary:
In-Distribution Forcing (ID-Forcing) is a test-time framework that prevents distribution drift in long video generation by using self-caching to construct key-value entries without attending to prior frames.

Why it matters: It enables existing short-horizon autoregressive video diffusion models to generate minute-scale videos without color, texture, or motion degradation, using only test-time interventions.

entry.title: Self-Generated Feedback Destabilizes Test-Time Training: A Causal Decomposition of Long-Horizon Adaptation
entry.summary:
Self-generated feedback during long-horizon test-time training destabilizes model predictions on independent text, a failure causally isolated and mitigated by evaluating updates on independent evidence before retention.

Why it matters: Test-time training on self-generated outputs requires validating updates against independent evidence to prevent model performance degradation over long context windows.

entry.title: Certification of Real Images through Calibrated Content Authentication
entry.summary:
A new deepfake detection paradigm certifies real images by assessing if authenticity is plausibly deniable based on calibrated faithful reconstruction by known generators, remaining robust against adversarial perturbations.

Why it matters: Traditional content-only deepfake detectors are fundamentally unreliable and fragile, whereas reconstruction-based calibrated certification provides a secure method to verify authentic real images despite advancing generative models.

entry.title: SearchJev: A Fast and Calibrated System-1 Model for Search Agents
entry.summary:
SearchJev is a fast System-1 model that directly scores search options without autoregressive generation, using Soft-Label Learning for Calibrated Decisions to handle fast decision-making in search agents.

Why it matters: Separating fast decision-making from generative reasoning significantly reduces search latency and improves calibration while enhancing overall answer accuracy in web-browsing agents.

entry.title: RobotUse: Allocating Computation, Context, and Decisions
entry.summary:
RobotUse is a robot agent harness that separates high-level visual action selection from backend motion planning, utilizing subagents and a persistent playbook to learn from execution.

Why it matters: It enables robot agents to make flexible, context-aware visual decisions while offloading spatial computation and retaining compact execution memories.

entry.title: OmniReasoning: Pushing the Limits of Audio-Visual Joint Reasoning
entry.summary:
OmniReasoning introduces a benchmark, an automated QA data engine, and an on-policy self-distillation method to significantly improve audio-visual joint reasoning in omni-modal models.

Why it matters: It establishes a structured paradigm to prevent omni-modal models from relying on single-modality shortcuts, improving deep cross-modal reasoning in complex video tasks.

entry.title: Noise Out, Bias In: Targeted Bias Injection in Diffusion Language Models via Closed-Loop Activation Steering
entry.summary:
A new targeted bias injection attack uses a proportional-integral (PI) controller to perform closed-loop activation steering across iterative denoising steps in masked diffusion language models.

Why it matters: The attack demonstrates that the iterative denoising trajectory of diffusion language models acts as a controllable attack surface, requiring bias evaluations to audit the active serving stack rather than just the frozen model weights.

entry.title: When to Switch: Reliable Action-Chunk Extension for Vision-Language-Action Models
entry.summary:
RACE improves Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model performance by predicting subskill transition timing via an auxiliary one-step denoising pass and conditioning action generation on it.

Why it matters: It enables smoother, faster, and more reliable robotic execution by allowing VLA models to use significantly longer action chunks without sacrificing manipulation accuracy.

entry.title: RealtimeWAM: One-Step Asynchronous World Action Models
entry.summary:
RealtimeWAM achieves an end-to-end speedup of up to 25x on an H100 with less than a 1% performance drop using one-step action generation and asynchronous expert execution.

Why it matters: It enables ultra-fast, real-time robotic action prediction from video-based World Action Models without sacrificing execution accuracy.

entry.title: Base Models Can Reason By Taking a Cue From Training Data
entry.summary:
Researchers show base language models can achieve RL-level reasoning performance simply by prefixing responses with specific starting token cues derived from associations learned during pretraining.

Why it matters: Understanding that reasoning capabilities can be unlocked via simple prompt cues reduces the necessity of complex reinforcement learning for certain tasks and highlights how pretraining data directly structures model behavior.

entry.title: PerturBot: Breaking Shortcut Priors in Vision-Language-Action Models with Perturbative Training
entry.summary:
PerturBot introduces a training and offline evaluation framework using perturbative data augmentation and GroundingFscore to eliminate modality shortcuts in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models without modifying inference architecture.

Why it matters: It prevents VLA models from failing in novel scenarios by ensuring model scaling reinforces genuine multi-modal task reasoning rather than memorized shortcut correlations.

entry.title: Dynamic Harness Search: Building Multi-Agent Systems Per-Query via Prediction
entry.summary:
SHIFT uses Monte Carlo tree search powered by a local LLM architect and learned value function to dynamically build optimal multi-agent harnesses per query without executing candidates at inference time.

Why it matters: It enables cost-effective, per-query customization of multi-agent workflows without incurring the runtime overhead of executing multiple candidate harnesses during inference.

entry.title: QuantCode Model: Specializing Language Models for Executable Algorithmic Trading Code
entry.summary:
QuantCode specializes LLMs for Backtrader algorithmic trading code generation using framework-specific continued pretraining and agent-validated supervised fine-tuning, evaluated on the new 400-task QuantCode-Bench.

Why it matters: The findings demonstrate that specialized execution frameworks require both domain pretraining and validated SFT to prevent capability degradation in multi-turn instruction following and tool usage.

entry.title: Base Models Can Reason By Taking a Cue From Training Data
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that base language models can achieve reasoning performance competitive with RL-tuned models simply by prepending specific token cues learned from training data.

Why it matters: It reveals that complex reasoning capabilities in RL-tuned models are largely latent behaviors in base models triggered by specific token associations formed during pretraining.

entry.title: Sharpen Without Search: On-Policy Distillation of Sequence-Level Power Distribution
entry.summary:
On-Policy Power Distillation (OPPD) uses a sequential Monte Carlo sampler to train a language model to directly generate sequence-level power-sharpened distributions, eliminating the need for test-time candidate search.

Why it matters: OPPD enables models to achieve the reasoning performance of computationally expensive multi-candidate power sampling within a single generation step, even without ground-truth reference answers.

entry.title: Balancing Memory Pathways: Analyzing and Improving Memory Utilization in Hybrid LMs
entry.summary:
Hybrid language models over-rely on attention pathways while underutilizing recurrent states, but an auxiliary loss restricting attention access forces better dual-memory pathway coordination and improves long-context task performance.

Why it matters: Architectural access to complementary memory systems is insufficient; models require explicit training objectives to prevent attention mechanisms from bottlenecking recurrent state utilization.

entry.title: You Changed Your Mind, The Model Didn't: Demystifying Intent in Multi-Turn Dialogue
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced Intent-Eval to benchmark language model performance under changing user intent and proposed Intent-OPSD, an on-policy self-distillation framework that mitigates performance degradation caused by mentioned-as-in-effect confusion.

Why it matters: Multi-turn conversational AI systems frequently fail when users alter or retract requirements, making intent-tracking frameworks like Intent-OPSD essential for reliable execution in dynamic workflows.

entry.title: Multimodal Safety Evaluation Should Measure Controllability Beyond Classification
entry.summary:
A new multimodal safety evaluation framework introduces controllability profiles using sparse feature decompositions to measure internal representation-level detectability, intervention sensitivity, and benign-preserving selectivity.

Why it matters: Future VLM safety benchmarks must measure whether safety-relevant internal signals can be controlled without damaging benign capability, rather than relying solely on classification accuracy.

entry.title: The Assistance Dilemma: Learning to Teach via Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
The Eduardo multi-turn RL training recipe introduces a masked near-transfer post-test and binary reward gates to train LLMs into effective tutors without resorting to answer-telling.

Why it matters: It enables smaller language models to match frontier-model tutoring benchmarks while significantly reducing latency and token costs for real-time interactive teaching.

entry.title: Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part II: Rethinking at Fixed Points
entry.summary:
A new framework for looped language models introduces learned depth priors and orthogonal input injection, improving performance while enabling efficient truncated backpropagation, terminal KV sharing, fast prefill, and accelerated RL updates.

Why it matters: These optimizations significantly reduce the computational and memory overhead of looped language models across training, decoding, prefill, and reinforcement learning without sacrificing model accuracy.

entry.title: How Sparse Probability Maps Shape Mixture-of-Experts Routing
entry.summary:
A study on top-2 MoE models reveals that sparse probability maps like entmax, sparsemax, and normmax co-adapt with learned score distributions during training, failing to lower validation loss but significantly boosting inference-time K-scaling robustness.

Why it matters: Adaptive MoE routing must be engineered around the co-adapted interaction between the probability map and learned score distributions rather than the map's theoretical sparsity alone.

entry.title: Learning What to Imitate: Entropy-Aware Distribution Mixing
entry.summary:
Entropy-Aware Mixing dynamically interpolates student and teacher distributions based on the student's predictive entropy to prevent confident conflicts and performance degradation during language model distillation.

Why it matters: It stabilizes knowledge distillation to improve mathematical reasoning in small language models while mitigating catastrophic forgetting of general capabilities.

entry.title: What Matters for Latent Reasoning with Flow Matching
entry.summary:
Flow-based Latent Reasoning (FLaRe) introduces a flow matching training recipe in learned latent space that enables language models to reason continuously across five key criteria: usefulness, diversity, explainability, refinability, and efficiency.

Why it matters: FLaRe demonstrates that flow matching in continuous latent spaces can match explicit step-by-step reasoning performance at a fraction of the computational latency.
